messages.author: 267c90d856baecb6
messages.subject: Incorporating numerous multipliers in dht2
parts:
Hi there! I am working with camera trap distance sampling. I want to incorporate another multiplier in the dht2 function along with time availability. The multiplier is stratified across the different Sample.Labels (camera traps), and it seems that dht2 does not allow for different rates across different sample locations. The error I get is below:

Error in these_weights %*% deltamethod[[i]]$variance : non-conformable arguments

Any suggestions? Thank you!

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Incorporating numerous multipliers in dht2
parts:
Libby

Might these be viewing angles that may differ between cameras and/or stations?

Seems like this question may have come up before, but I don't remember exactly. Off the top of my head, I wonder what would happen if you gave a vector of values to the dht2 argument "sample_fraction".

Ah-ha. Documentation for that argument says you can specify a data frame

sample_fraction
proportion of the transect covered (e.g., 0.5 for one-sided line transects). May be specified as either a single number or a data.frame with 2 columns Sample.Label and fraction (if fractions are different for each transect).

Does that help your cause?

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Incorporating numerous multipliers in dht2
parts:
Hi Eric! Thank you for your quick response. 

That does help... I have one angle that is measured from the walk test of the camera so it takes into account things that may be blocking detection (like trees). Then I have the actual angle of the camera lens. My idea was to "standardize" that FOV as a multiplier in dht2. 

I guess I could use that in the sample_fraction argument, and just leave the multiplier as time availability.

Does that make sense? Thanks for your help :)
